note: Editorial config for the Buzz tab. Sources come from nba-content-stream's published feed; this file decides which of them reach a reader, how they are labelled, and whether their body text is rendered. Edit this file rather than js/buzz.js.
excerpt_note: excerpt:false means the item's body_excerpt is NOT rendered. google-news repeats the headline plus the outlet name, which adds nothing. youtube descriptions carry sportsbook affiliate links and promo codes, which must never render on a HoopsHype-adjacent page.
google_news_note: Off, at Jorge's call: a wire feed of other outlets' headlines is not what this feed is for, and the items carried no body text worth reading. Flip on:true to bring it back. outlet_allow, when non-empty, keeps only items from those exact outlet names — ["HoopsHype"] would bring back HoopsHype's own stories and nothing else.
excerpt_chars_note: How much body text a source may render. Reddit gets the most: the opening paragraph of a stats post or an archive find is the item, not a headline about it. Cut at a sentence, then a paragraph, then a word — never mid-word.
reddit_note: The index cuts a Reddit body at ~280 characters. The full selftext comes through nba-content-stream's existing CORS proxy Worker, which already allowlists reddit.com — no Worker change, one more caller, and exactly one request per page load because /api/info.json takes every post id at once. It also carries the score, the comment count, and the over_18 / removed flags, which is how a removed or NSFW post gets dropped instead of rendered. Set enrich_reddit:false, or cors_proxy:null, and the index excerpt stands.
enrich_note: Bluesky's public AppView, called straight from the reader's browser with no auth and no proxy — the same host nba-content-stream calls. One request per 25 posts. It supplies the full post text (the index truncates), facets (which turn Bluesky's display-shortened links back into real links), the author's avatar, and the quoted post. Best-effort: set enrich_bluesky:false, or let it fail, and the cards render from the index instead.
trending_top_note: How many of trending.json's ranked items wear the TRENDING badge. The file holds 40; badging all of them makes the badge mean nothing, since the per-source caps fill mostly from that list anyway.
drop_truncated_note: Google News headlines arrive cut off at a fixed width and end in an ellipsis, and there is no body text to finish the sentence. Bluesky and Reddit posts end in an ellipsis on purpose, so the rule is per source.
require_entity_note: An item must carry at least one player or team tag. This is the single most effective quality filter: the accounts Content Stream follows post about their own lives and other sports between NBA posts, and 29 of 100 items in a sample carried no NBA entity at all — baseball chatter, podcast plugs and personal jokes. Set false on a source to let its untagged items through.
off_topic_note: Google News tagging is name-based, so an MLB story about Spencer Jones is tagged with the Thunder rookie of the same name. An item carrying any of these words is dropped. Two groups: other-league jargon (a word no NBA story uses, which catches a baseball column that never names its team) and other-league team names. Deliberately excludes every word that is also an NBA nickname: Kings, Hawks, Nets, Heat, Magic, Suns, Bulls and the rest, and every word both sports share: rookie, draft, trade, playoffs.
